rows.mechanism: The production evidence splits by sub-practice. Gains are consistent in regeneration-based farmland and in the cross-family syntheses, while planted silvoarable, silvopastoral, boundary and shaded perennial (coffee and cocoa) systems record both gains and losses. Meta-analyses report higher crop yield under agroforestry than controls in sub-Saharan Africa and higher soil nitrogen stocks than crop monocultures in the humid tropics, with soil nitrogen used here as a component of the production gap [ev_crop_yield_kuyah19_1, ev_soil_nitrogen_muchane20_1]. A meta-analysis cited in Arslan et al. (Branca et al.) associates agroforestry techniques with a 69% increase in cereal yields across the studies it consulted [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_14]. In the Sahel, millet yields are reported to double or triple under Faidherbia albida and yields were higher where intensive FMNR is practised, and tree shade in pastures is associated with gains in milk production and weight gain [ev_crop_yield_faosen24_8, ev_crop_yield_seghieri19_14, ev_livestock_productivity_murg13_4]. On paired on-farm plots in Ethiopia, wheat under Faidherbia albida crowns yielded 23-26% more grain than open-field wheat in the normal seasons of 2013 and 2014, and up to 85% more in 2015, an El Niño year in which both yields were low; available N close to the crowns was 35-55% larger than under sole wheat [ev_crop_yield_sida18_1, ev_crop_yield_sida18_2, ev_soil_nitrogen_sida18_1]. WOCAT practitioner ratings for FMNR in Kenya and assisted natural regeneration in Burkina Faso record higher crop and fodder production, the Kenyan compiler adding that well-managed FMNR land gives more and better-quality fodder than unmanaged land [ev_crop_yield_wocat_507_2019_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_1358_2017_crop_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_507_2019_fodder_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1358_2017_fodder_production]. Lower yield variability under more diverse shade is cited as a sign of greater yield resistance to shocks in shaded systems, and Kenyan agroforestry-project farmers in Lower Nyando raised farm productivity against a control group [ev_crop_yield_morel24_4, ev_agricultural_production_value_thorlak12_1]. Fertilizer trees raise maize output: in Malawi, adopters had a 35% higher value of food crop production and 32% higher maize productivity than their counterfactual, and a review notes fertilizer tree species are widely documented to substantially increase maize yields compared with maize grown without fertilizer in Zambia and across Africa [ev_agricultural_production_value_coulibaly16_1, ev_crop_yield_coulibaly16_1, ev_crop_yield_lasco14_1]. In maize–Gliricidia trials run for 12-13 consecutive years in Malawi and Zambia, the intercrop gave the most stable yield at Makoka and more stable yields than fertilized maize at Msekera, and the intercrop with 50% of the recommended N and P fertilizer matched the yield of fully fertilized monoculture maize [ev_yield_stability_sileshi12_1, ev_yield_stability_sileshi12_2, ev_crop_yield_sileshi12_2]. Maize yields were more stable with Leucaena hedgerows than in monocrop, as also shown for alley cropping and fertilizer trees [ev_yield_stability_lasco14_1]. In Maradi, Niger, millet yields rose by 120 to 209 kg/ha where FMNR was older than 6 years, with smaller increases for younger FMNR, and FMNR is estimated to have raised yields by an average of 100 kg/ha over 5 million hectares [ev_crop_yield_abasse23_1, ev_crop_yield_abasse23_3]. In Lempira, Honduras, the Quesungual system raised maize yields from 1.9 to 3.2 tonnes per hectare and bean yields from 0.8 to 2.0 tonnes per hectare, and its crops withstood the severe 1997 drought that caused losses for non-adopters [ev_crop_yield_chaudhury11_1, ev_crop_yield_chaudhury11_2, ev_crop_yield_chaudhury11_3]. Under Sahelian parkland trees, tuber yield is improved (+0.40 to +1.67 t ha-1) and legumes are less affected than cereals, and tree fodder is crucial in the dry season and during drought [ev_crop_yield_bayala14_1, ev_forage_productivity_bayala14_1]. A meta-analysis of Chinese farmland shelterbelts found crop yield 16.57% higher within sheltered farmland [ev_crop_yield_hao26_1]. In subarctic Ontario, a site lined by willow windbreaks produced about 300 g/m2 of bean pods against about 60 g/m2 at an open site, and potato tuber yield was 33% greater (3200 versus 2400 g/m2) [ev_crop_yield_barbeau18_1, ev_crop_yield_barbeau18_2]. In Colombian intensive silvopasture, milk production was 32.1% higher than with the same grasses without shrubs or trees, milk per hectare rose from 2 540 to 4 528 L a year with Leucaena, and silvopasture is cited as producing 12 times more beef than traditional grazing [ev_livestock_productivity_montagnini15_3, ev_livestock_productivity_saucedo23_1, ev_livestock_productivity_saucedo23_3]. Intensive silvopasture raises stocking rates up to four times above extensive grazing and with them meat and milk output per hectare [ev_livestock_productivity_montagnini15_1]. In Colombia, a Leucaena-based silvopastoral system raised stocking to 4.3 cows ha-1 while eliminating chemical fertiliser [ev_livestock_productivity_cisneros24_1]. In Colombia, forage production in a silvopastoral system of pastures, trees and Leucaena shrubs stayed constant in periods of intense drought while biomass in grass monoculture fell to 25%, and deep-rooted silvopasture trees are more drought-tolerant and give more stable forage volumes in the dry season [ev_forage_productivity_cisneros24_1, ev_forage_productivity_saucedo23_1]. Cattle in intensive silvopasture are better fed in critical drought periods, which reduces seasonal reproduction crises [ev_livestock_productivity_montagnini15_2]. During El Niño events, milk production fell by 2.2% in silvopastoral systems against 4.9% in conventional systems [ev_livestock_productivity_guaqueta25_1]. At El Hatico, Colombia, the switch to intensive silvopasture allowed pasture irrigation to be dropped, and in 2009, the year with the lowest rainfall in several decades (440 mm), milk production still rose 10% on the previous year [ev_livestock_productivity_montagnini15_4]. Milk production rose 29% for cows on pasture with high tree density compared with low tree cover and above 15% in silvopasture compared with full sun, and dry-season weight gains were 2 to 5% higher on high tree-density pasture [ev_livestock_productivity_navas10_1, ev_livestock_productivity_navas10_2, ev_livestock_productivity_navas10_3]. In shaded coffee and cocoa, a coffee meta-analysis found agroforestry reduced the odds of climate-related yield loss (OR = 0.69) and a cocoa meta-analysis found total system yields about ten times higher than in monocultures [ev_crop_yield_patil25_1, ev_crop_yield_niether20_2].
rows.conditionality: The sub-practices disagree, so the roll-up states conflicting evidence rather than a strong gain. On the gain side, regeneration-based farmland (Faidherbia albida and Piliostigma reticulatum parklands, FMNR in Niger and Ghana, the Quesungual system) and the cross-family meta-analyses and assessments show higher yields or soil nitrogen [ev_crop_yield_faosen24_9, ev_crop_yield_seghieri19_15, ev_crop_yield_abasse23_1, ev_crop_yield_talensi21_1, ev_crop_yield_chaudhury11_1, ev_crop_yield_kuyah19_1, ev_soil_nitrogen_muchane20_1, ev_crop_yield_morel24_4]. On the conflicting side, shaded perennial systems pair those system-level gains with main-crop losses: cocoa yields 25% lower than in monocultures, coffee and cocoa yield per hectare 26% lower than conventional systems, and coffee yields declining under >60% shade, while shade did not prevent the drought-induced cocoa yield decline in a Ghanaian experiment [ev_crop_yield_niether20_1, ev_crop_yield_jezeer17_1, ev_crop_yield_patil25_3, ev_crop_yield_mensah23_2]; the separator there is whether the by-crops are counted and how dense the shade is, and the units are crop-specific to coffee, cocoa and coconut. Planted silvoarable systems pair fertilizer-tree and Gliricidia gains with tree–crop competition losses; silvopasture pairs Latin American milk and stocking gains with a global review's losses under dispersed trees; and boundary planting pairs higher yields within sheltered farmland with losses at shelterbelt edges and in windbreak paddocks [ev_crop_yield_coulibaly16_1, ev_yield_stability_sileshi12_2, ev_crop_yield_watts22_10, ev_crop_yield_dsantos23_3, ev_livestock_productivity_montagnini15_3, ev_livestock_productivity_baker25h2_14, ev_crop_yield_hao26_1, ev_crop_yield_hao26_2, ev_crop_yield_baker25h2_1]. The separator, in the sources' own terms, is spacing, tree density, tree age and distance from the tree line: alley spacings under 10 TH were predicted to reduce yields, pasture yield fell as tree density rose and under the oldest trees, livestock yield fell with more trees and older trees, and yield losses were reported up to 10 m from hedges in the rainy season and in shelterbelt edge zones [ev_crop_yield_baker25h2_7, ev_forage_productivity_baker25h2_10, ev_forage_productivity_baker25h2_12, ev_livestock_productivity_baker25h2_15, ev_livestock_productivity_baker25h2_16, ev_crop_yield_faosen24_13, ev_crop_yield_hao26_2]. The global review's main text gives no country or income-group breakdown, so its losses cannot be placed against the LIC/LMIC target [ev_crop_yield_baker25h2_1]. The evidence pulls both ways: tree–crop competition for water delayed Kenyan maize and could cause crop failure, intercropped wheat in China and soybean in Brazil yielded less than monocultures, groundnut and millet yields fell under Cordyla pinnata in Senegal, and excess shade can reduce pasture productivity [ev_crop_yield_watts22_10, ev_crop_yield_dsantos23_3, ev_crop_yield_santos25_5, ev_crop_yield_faosen24_11, ev_livestock_productivity_moran18_14]. The pooled magnitude combines a crop-yield response ratio with a soil-nitrogen response ratio, and a systematic review's pooled crop-yield effect across agroforestry interventions had a confidence interval spanning zero [ev_crop_yield_kuyah19_1, ev_soil_nitrogen_muchane20_1, ev_crop_yield_castle21s_1]. The WOCAT units are compiler judgements on documented technology sheets, not yield measurements [ev_crop_yield_wocat_507_2019_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_1358_2017_crop_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_507_2019_fodder_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1358_2017_fodder_production]. The Lower Nyando productivity gain had large standard errors and was not significant, earlier work cited in a temperate alley-cropping study found greater crop yield losses near shelterbelts in dry years, and the yield-variability finding is a cited statement [ev_agricultural_production_value_thorlak12_1, ev_crop_yield_majaura25_3, ev_crop_yield_morel24_4]. Gains are not universal: Malawian non-adopters would have lost food crop value had they adopted fertilizer trees, at Msekera fertilized monoculture maize out-yielded the maize–Gliricidia intercrop, and some stability models there ranked unfertilized control maize as more stable than the intercrop [ev_agricultural_production_value_coulibaly16_2, ev_crop_yield_sileshi12_1, ev_yield_stability_sileshi12_3]. The Malawi estimates come from an ICRAF working paper evaluating an ICRAF-promoted technology, and the Gliricidia trials compare against fertilized maize rather than farmer practice [ev_crop_yield_coulibaly16_1, ev_crop_yield_sileshi12_1]. Cereals often lose: in Maradi, FMNR did not significantly increase grain yields, the income gain being attributed to crop diversification instead, and under parkland trees cereal grain yield ranged from a loss of 0.54 t ha-1 under Balanites aegyptiaca to a gain of 0.24 t ha-1 under F. albida, with reductions attributed to competition for light, nutrients and water [ev_crop_yield_haglund11_1, ev_crop_yield_bayala14_1]. The Niger yield figures are earlier estimates cited in a grey-literature review, and the Honduran yields are before-and-after case-study figures for a slash-and-mulch system [ev_crop_yield_abasse23_1, ev_crop_yield_abasse23_3, ev_crop_yield_chaudhury11_1]. Next to the trees the effect reverses: crop yield in shelterbelt edge zones fell by an average of 20.47% [ev_crop_yield_hao26_2]. In the West African Sahel, live fences and fodder banks reduced yields in the first year, which recovered in the second [ev_crop_yield_lasco14_2]. Tree density matters: dense Acacia decurrens silvopasture gave 14.3 L of milk per cow per day against 15 L in the open field [ev_livestock_productivity_saucedo23_2]. The Latin American livestock units are earlier studies cited in Spanish-language reviews or a CATIE edited volume; the El Hatico milk result is a single farm compared year on year and the Colombian forage result likely describes the same farm [ev_livestock_productivity_saucedo23_1, ev_livestock_productivity_montagnini15_4, ev_forage_productivity_cisneros24_1]. The Costa Rican livestock units are high-income evidence [ev_livestock_productivity_navas10_2, ev_livestock_productivity_navas10_3]. A global quantitative review against treeless controls found average losses for windbreaks, alleys and dispersed trees: windbreak paddocks −8.3%, alleys −17.63%, pasture under dispersed trees −20.8% and livestock there −18.6%, with gains only at wide spacings (+13% at 15 tree heights between alleys, +8.04% across a windbreak paddock 20 tree heights wide) [ev_crop_yield_baker25h2_1, ev_crop_yield_baker25h2_6, ev_forage_productivity_baker25h2_9, ev_livestock_productivity_baker25h2_14, ev_crop_yield_baker25h2_8, ev_crop_yield_baker25h2_5]. The cited 69% cereal-yield figure reaches this row second-hand through Arslan et al.: the citing text does not describe the agroforestry techniques further and reports no significance [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_14]. Of the newer primary studies, regeneration-based farmland again holds the stronger result: The Ethiopian drought-year gain stays separate from the normal-season gain; at the same site soil total N did not differ significantly under and outside the canopy at the end of the 2013 season despite the larger available N near the crowns, and the yield benefit of canopy cooling is modelled and appeared only with applied N [ev_crop_yield_sida18_1, ev_crop_yield_sida18_2, ev_soil_nitrogen_sida18_2, ev_crop_yield_sida18_3, ev_crop_yield_sida18_4]. The Ontario windbreak gain is high-income boreal evidence from a single windbreak-lined site against a single open site, with plots irrigated from ditches, so it does not test the water competition near trees that drives the dry-year losses [ev_crop_yield_barbeau18_1, ev_crop_yield_barbeau18_2]. In southern Malawi a Tephrosia vogelii relay intercrop, which produces leafy residues but no grain, gave the same quantity of maize grain as monoculture maize fertilised in the same way, so no yield gain [ev_crop_yield_snapp10_1].

rows.mechanism: Household income, economic return and food security are used as proxies for rural poverty [ev_household_income_castle21s_1, ev_economic_return_faosen24_15, ev_food_security_castle21s_1]. Positive results include Senegalese FMNR households earning more from non-timber products than non-adopters, calliandra fodder raising dairy farmers' net income in Kenya and Uganda, Vi Agroforestry advice raising Kenyan dietary diversity, and a windbreak hedge in Senegalese irrigated rice with an internal rate of return of 36 per cent [ev_household_income_seghieri19_12, ev_household_income_kiptot11_1, ev_food_security_castle21s_1, ev_economic_return_faosen24_15]. WOCAT practitioner ratings for FMNR in Kenya and assisted natural regeneration in Burkina Faso record higher farm income and food security, the Kenyan compiler crediting new income from wood, honey, medicinal and other non-wood products and more diversified livelihoods that reduce the risk of food insecurity [ev_household_income_wocat_507_2019_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1358_2017_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_507_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_1358_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Both sheets also rate the long-term returns on establishment and maintenance costs as positive to very positive [ev_economic_return_wocat_1358_2017_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_507_2019_costbenefit_maintenance_long]. Across World Vision FMNR projects, participant households were nine percentage points more likely than non-participants to report a decrease in poverty in their communities, reported similarly by poorer and female-headed households [ev_rural_poverty_wvfmnr19_10]. In Rwanda, tree products are a safety net: food-insecure farmers more often sold tree products for income than food-secure farmers, and tree density was positively associated with food security in some agroecologies [ev_household_income_ndoli21_1, ev_food_security_ndoli21_1]. In Nyando District, Kenya, agroforestry-project households typically used fewer detrimental coping strategies during hunger periods, sold fuel wood and timber to buy food during the drought, relied on tree fruit when floods washed crops away, and in Lower Nyando held more livestock wealth than control households [ev_food_security_thorlak12_2, ev_household_income_thorlak12_1, ev_food_security_thorlak12_1, ev_household_income_thorlak12_2]. In Maradi, Niger, FMNR adoption increased gross annual household income by between 46 and 56 USD per capita compared with propensity-matched non-adopters, and the annual benefit-cost ratio of practising FMNR was estimated at between 2.5 and 3.0 [ev_household_income_haglund11_1, ev_economic_return_haglund11_1]. In south-central Niger, sales of fuelwood and service wood from FMNR raise the income of all social categories, even the vulnerable and very vulnerable, and the net present value of FMNR at 10% over 20 years was €772 per hectare [ev_household_income_abasse23_1, ev_economic_return_abasse23_1]. Fertilizer trees limit financial risk in drought years: where a crop fails, farmers using inorganic fertilizer lose the US$164 spent on the input, against US$90 for farmers who planted fertilizer trees [ev_economic_return_chaudhury11_1]. In a Mozambique carbon-forestry scheme promoting almost exclusively agroforestry, overall household income was generally increased [ev_household_income_lasco14_1]. In Colombia, intensive silvopasture had an operating benefit-cost ratio of 2.8 against 1.34 for a traditional system, and producer income from milk sales was 42.12% higher than under pasture monoculture owing to a higher carrying capacity [ev_economic_return_saucedo23_1, ev_household_income_montagnini15_1]. A global systematic review of nature-based solutions for food security counts three cited population-survey studies finding positive results in food access where agroforestry was applied in southern Africa, Brazil and China over periods of up to 20 years [ev_food_security_nguy24n_1]. In the Nepal mid-hills, after a market-oriented agroforestry project of fodder-tree hedgerows and understorey cash crops, bundled with marketing support, training, seed subsidies and organic fertiliser, the share of participating households below the poverty line dropped from 48 % to 34 %, the share that was food sufficient rose from 52% to 69%, and the average farm-income figure rose from 37 to 48 percent, mainly from understorey crops, while off-farm income changed by -9% [ev_rural_poverty_pandit19_1, ev_food_security_pandit19_1, ev_household_income_pandit19_1]. In southern Malawi, under higher fertiliser prices the value-cost ratio of a Tephrosia vogelii relay intercrop with maize stayed above 4.0, which the authors call a profitable scenario, while the higher prices pulled monoculture maize down to 2.5 or less [ev_economic_return_snapp10_1]. In shaded coffee and cocoa, a meta-analysis found the average net return of shaded systems significantly higher by 23% than conventional systems [ev_economic_return_jezeer17_1], a case cited second-hand found a coffee price crash cut sun-coffee net revenue far more than that of extensive agroforestry [ev_economic_return_jezeer17_3], and a farm model for Costa Rica and Guatemala found smaller losses for high-shade systems under a 50% coffee price fall [ev_economic_return_lalani24_2].
rows.conditionality: Results are mixed: a systematic review's pooled income effect is small and not statistically significant, crop–fruit tree intercropping in China lowered gross household income, silvopasture income lags traditional pasture in the first years, and Regreening Africa found average tree-product income unchanged [ev_household_income_castle21s_1, ev_household_income_castle21s_2, ev_economic_return_diasf08_1, ev_household_income_rgaf23_6]. Several positive units are self-evaluations, bundled-project results or a modelled business case, and the proxies measure income or returns rather than poverty itself [ev_household_income_wvfmnr19_5, ev_food_security_talensi21_3, ev_household_income_cmscr20_6]. The WOCAT units are compiler judgements on documented technology sheets, not household survey results, and like the other units they measure income or food security as proxies for poverty [ev_household_income_wocat_507_2019_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1358_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency]. The cost-benefit ratings are compiler judgements on a very-negative to very-positive scale, not measured returns [ev_economic_return_wocat_507_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1358_2017_costbenefit_maintenance_long]. The Colombian sustainable-ranching completion report found no measured poverty reduction at closing, because many silvopastoral systems were still in their establishment phase and project effects could not be separated from drought and other climatic events [ev_rural_poverty_cmscr20_9]. The World Vision poverty result is a self-reported community perception from participants [ev_rural_poverty_wvfmnr19_10]. The Rwandan effect varied by agroecology: more trees went with higher food security in Congo Nile but lower food security in the Buberuka Highlands [ev_food_security_ndoli21_2]. The Lower Nyando livestock-wealth difference, used by the authors as an income surrogate, was not significant at conventional levels, and the timber-sales and flood-fruit findings are farmer-reported [ev_household_income_thorlak12_2, ev_household_income_thorlak12_1, ev_food_security_thorlak12_1]. In Maradi, FMNR did not appear to reduce the number of months of perceived food shortage [ev_food_security_haglund11_1]. The Maradi income and benefit-cost figures come from a matched survey comparison, while the fuelwood and net-present-value figures are cited in a grey-literature review [ev_household_income_haglund11_1, ev_household_income_abasse23_1, ev_economic_return_abasse23_1]. The Zambian loss comparison and Mozambique result are earlier findings cited in a working paper and a review [ev_economic_return_chaudhury11_1, ev_household_income_lasco14_1]. The Colombian ratio and milk-income figures are earlier studies cited in a Spanish-language systematic review and a CATIE edited volume [ev_economic_return_saucedo23_1, ev_household_income_montagnini15_1]. The food-access vote count comes from a low-tier systematic review that included only studies showing improvement in at least one food-security dimension, so its positive count is guaranteed by its inclusion rule and says nothing about studies that found no benefit; of its three cited studies, one is a life-cycle assessment rather than a population survey and another is not clearly agroforestry [ev_food_security_nguy24n_1]. The Nepal results come from a bundled project and are not credited in full to the trees: they are a before-and-after recall survey of participating households with no control group, and the share of the bundle due to agroforestry is not stated [ev_rural_poverty_pandit19_1, ev_food_security_pandit19_1, ev_household_income_pandit19_1]. The Malawian value-cost ratio is a fertiliser-price scenario on on-farm trial data, not measured household income [ev_economic_return_snapp10_1]. The shaded coffee and cocoa evidence also pulls both ways: in Guayas, Ecuador, technified cacao monoculture earned a higher net margin per hectare than organic or traditional cacao agroforestry [ev_economic_return_perezneira16_1, ev_economic_return_perezneira16_2], a pan-tropical cocoa meta-analysis found higher total system production not reflected in higher revenues or net present values [ev_economic_return_niether20_1, ev_household_income_niether20_1], and after Hurricane Stan coffee management had no effect on economic losses in Mexico [ev_economic_return_philpott08_1]; these units are crop-specific, and the price-fall result is modelled [ev_economic_return_lalani24_2].

rows.mechanism: A sub-Saharan meta-analysis found agroforestry five and ten times better than controls for runoff and soil loss respectively [ev_erosion_hazard_kuyah19_1]. A pantropical meta-analysis found agroforestry trees reduced soil erosion by 50% against crop monocultures, and stated mechanisms include greater soil cover and structure protecting against raindrop impact, roots aiding infiltration and reducing surface runoff, and live fences lowering runoff velocity; runoff reduction is used as a component [ev_erosion_hazard_muchane20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_santos25_2, ev_runoff_reduction_watts22_2, ev_erosion_hazard_moran18_5]. WOCAT practitioner ratings add reduced soil loss and surface runoff under assisted natural regeneration in Burkina Faso, and less downstream siltation of ponds and water pans under FMNR in Kenya owing to less wind and water erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1358_2017_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1358_2017_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_507_2019_downstream_siltation]. In Lower Nyando, Kenya, farmers reported that tree roots prevented extensive soil erosion and soil fertility loss during the floods [ev_erosion_hazard_thorlak12_1]. During Hurricane Mitch in October 1998, Honduran farmers practising the Quesungual system suffered less landslide damage than those using traditional slash-and-burn [ev_erosion_hazard_chaudhury11_1]. In Costa Rica and Nicaragua, runoff equalled 28-48% of rainfall on pastures without trees against less than 10% in silvopastoral systems [ev_runoff_reduction_montagnini15_1]. Runoff was higher on grass pasture than in tree-dominated fodder banks, so tree cover attenuates runoff and the soil erosion it causes [ev_runoff_reduction_cisneros24_1]. Within single sub-practices, live fences of Gliricidia sepium are used to prevent erosion, shade trees attenuate runoff and erosion by close to a factor of two against full-sun plots, and in Colombia's Coffee Ecoregion erosion under silvopasture was 35.3 percent lower than on degraded pasture soils [ev_erosion_hazard_moran18_2, ev_runoff_reduction_seghieri19_3, ev_erosion_hazard_cmscr20_1]. In shaded perennial systems, a study on a Costa Rican coffee farm found shade trees reduced sheet erosion by a factor of 2 against full-sun plots [ev_erosion_hazard_seghieri19_1], and after Hurricane Stan in Chiapas, Mexico, coffee farms with more complex vegetation suffered less landslide damage [ev_erosion_hazard_philpott08_10].
rows.conditionality: The class follows the sub-practice vote, which tempers the pooled result: the large effect sizes come from the cross-family meta-analyses, which hold the strongest result, regeneration-based farmland (FMNR and assisted natural regeneration evidence, the Quesungual landslide result) reads moderate, and boundary planting, shaded perennial systems and silvopasture each read weaker on their own evidence, so the NbS-level class sits at the slight reading shared by boundary planting, shaded perennial systems and silvopasture rather than at the meta-analyses' strong one [ev_erosion_hazard_kuyah19_1, ev_erosion_hazard_muchane20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_wvfmnr19_3, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1358_2017_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_chaudhury11_1, ev_t3_flood_erosion_quandt17_6, ev_runoff_reduction_seghieri19_3, ev_erosion_hazard_villa20_11, ev_erosion_hazard_cmscr20_1]. The shade-tree effect represents little at catchment scale on the andisols studied [ev_runoff_reduction_seghieri19_3]. Silvopasture's weaker reading reflects spread between sites: erosion fell 35.3 percent in Colombia's Coffee Ecoregion but only 5.4 percent in the Cesar River Valley [ev_erosion_hazard_cmscr20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_cmscr20_2]. The sub-Saharan authors warn the very large effect sizes could reflect publication bias and expect more modest effects with more studies [ev_erosion_hazard_kuyah19_1]. Regreening Africa observed no large overall change in erosion prevalence and found no link between more trees on farm and lower erosion, the FMNR result is participants' reported erosion, and the Nicaraguan hurricane result bundles trees with terraces and contour planting [ev_erosion_hazard_rgaf23_3, ev_erosion_hazard_rgaf23_5, ev_erosion_hazard_wvfmnr19_3, ev_erosion_hazard_philpott08_9]. The WOCAT units are compiler judgements on documented technology sheets, not erosion measurements, and the runoff and siltation ratings enter as components [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1358_2017_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1358_2017_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_507_2019_downstream_siltation]. The Lower Nyando erosion finding is farmer-reported, not measured [ev_erosion_hazard_thorlak12_1]. The landslide and runoff results are earlier studies cited in a working paper, a CATIE edited volume and a Spanish-language review; the runoff units enter as components of erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_chaudhury11_1, ev_runoff_reduction_montagnini15_1, ev_runoff_reduction_cisneros24_1]. The Chiapas landslide results are crop-specific coffee evidence from a single hurricane, with the landslide-volume and landslide-size trends only marginal (P = 0.062) and no effect of nearby forest cover [ev_erosion_hazard_philpott08_3, ev_erosion_hazard_philpott08_5, ev_erosion_hazard_philpott08_4].

at_a_glance.statement_short: Agroforestry → water quality risk: not enough evidence to state a class (1 source, none measured)

rows.mechanism: The measured soil-water evidence points both ways, and timing and soil depth separate the two sides. On the positive side, a sub-Saharan meta-analysis finds that agroforestry improved infiltration and soil moisture content compared to the control (RR 1.6 for soil moisture, with 70% of soil-moisture observations above RR 1) [ev_soil_water_retention_kuyah19_1], and in a German alley-cropping trial in a drought year soil water content remained lower on the open field than in the alley-cropping system [ev_soil_water_retention_majaura25_1]. In a Gliricidia + maize trial at Makoka, Malawi, available water content tended to be greater in the gliricidia + maize + pigeonpea system at the peak of the recharge phase, which the authors attribute to increased infiltration and reduced soil evaporation under greater ground cover [ev_soil_moisture_chirwa07_10], and in the second season's May water content in that system was much greater than in all other treatments at depths below 60 cm [ev_soil_moisture_chirwa07_8]. Water use efficiency was also higher in the tree systems in every season, for example 1.97 against 0.15 g of biomass per kg of water for gliricidia + maize against sole maize in 1998/99 [ev_rain_water_productivity_chirwa07_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_chirwa07_2, ev_rain_water_productivity_chirwa07_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_chirwa07_4, ev_rain_water_productivity_chirwa07_5, ev_rain_water_productivity_chirwa07_6]. On the negative side, under Faidherbia albida parkland in Ethiopia soil moisture in the sub-soil was the least for wheat with tree, intermediate for sole tree and the highest for open field [ev_soil_water_retention_sida18_1]; in cocoa, a pan-tropical meta-analysis found soils under agroforestry significantly lower in volumetric water content than under full-sun monocultures [ev_soil_water_retention_niether20_1]; at Makoka the lower available soil water at the beginning of the cropping season in the tree-based systems suggests that the trees continued to deplete moisture during the dry season [ev_soil_moisture_chirwa07_2], the March-to-August decline was most pronounced in the tree-based systems [ev_soil_moisture_chirwa07_3], water content was slightly lower under gliricidia + maize in the dry season when the trees were left unpruned [ev_soil_moisture_chirwa07_5], and in the first season's May water content under gliricidia + maize + pigeonpea was lower than in all other treatments below 60 cm [ev_soil_moisture_chirwa07_4]. Trees therefore draw down dry-season and subsoil water, while recharge-season soil water and whole-system water productivity favour them. Several measurements found no difference: topsoil moisture did not vary under Faidherbia [ev_soil_water_retention_sida18_2], and at Makoka the distribution of water in the profile was generally comparable in all cropping systems [ev_soil_moisture_chirwa07_1], with no significant treatment effects in the second season, in the second season's October, or in December and January of the third season [ev_soil_moisture_chirwa07_6, ev_soil_moisture_chirwa07_7, ev_soil_moisture_chirwa07_9]; the authors conclude that gliricidia pruned before and during the cropping season does not provoke undue competition for water with associated crops [ev_soil_moisture_chirwa07_11]. WOCAT practitioner ratings add improved water harvesting under assisted natural regeneration in Burkina Faso, and increased water availability under FMNR in Kenya, where the compiler credits greater water retention that raises groundwater levels [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1358_2017_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_507_2019_water_availability]. Rainfall over agricultural land can also shift with continental land cover, increasing with more upwind tree cover [ev_water_regulation_vannoordwijk21_4].
rows.conditionality: The sub-practice rows disagree, so this roll-up states the conflict rather than a pooled direction: the meta-analysis carries the cross-family row positive, the Malawi Gliricidia trial (with the German trial) carries the planted silvoarable row positive, and the Faidherbia subsoil depletion and the cocoa soil-water deficit carry the regeneration-farmland and shaded-perennial rows negative [ev_soil_water_retention_kuyah19_1, ev_soil_moisture_chirwa07_10, ev_soil_water_retention_sida18_1, ev_soil_water_retention_niether20_1]. The separator is timing and depth: trees deplete soil water through the dry season and below the topsoil, so less may be available when the crop is sown, while recharge-season water and system water productivity favour the tree plots [ev_soil_moisture_chirwa07_2, ev_soil_moisture_chirwa07_4, ev_soil_moisture_chirwa07_10]. Management matters: the Malawi conclusion holds for gliricidia pruned before and during the cropping season [ev_soil_moisture_chirwa07_11], and the Ethiopian parkland trees were heavily pruned on farmers' fields [ev_soil_water_retention_sida18_1]. The Makoka water use efficiency figures are total above-ground biomass of the whole system, trees and crops together, per unit of seasonal water use, not grain per unit of water [ev_rain_water_productivity_chirwa07_1]; the tree biomass inflates the tree-system figures, and the authors caution that soil evaporation and water-table uptake were not measured, so the gap is probably overstated. These units therefore count here, for water stress, and are held out of the production gap because they say nothing about crop yield. The German result counts little: it is a temperate high-income trial whose differences were not significant at all positions, and it measured surface soil only [ev_soil_water_retention_majaura25_1]. The WOCAT units are compiler judgements on documented technology sheets, not soil-moisture measurements, and stay on water access rather than soil moisture [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1358_2017_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_507_2019_water_availability]. The upwind-rainfall shift is a continental-scale effect, not a field-scale one [ev_water_regulation_vannoordwijk21_4]. Infiltration and groundwater-recharge findings for catchments are carried in the agroforestry catchment water yield rows. The cocoa unit is crop-specific and does not measure crop water stress directly [ev_soil_water_retention_niether20_1].
rows.statement: agroforestry water_stress: CONFLICTING EVIDENCE — material weight on both the positive and the negative side, so no direction is stated. This is not a null finding: studies found real effects, in opposite directions, and the agreement note lists both sides. Read the conditionality for what separates them (transfer: in_context).
